reason: Real Windows Product Experience UAT at exact candidate 374164f002e723299e0c4123aacea309e32f5ceb passed the repaired Electron Git LFS identity gate but then failed closed before product launch during dependency preparation. Three independent npm ci attempts fail identically in node-pty@1.1.0 after node-gyp rebuild is selected, with MSBuild MSB8040 for Spectre-mitigated C++ libraries. The captured lifecycle evidence shows the source UAT is using ambient C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe v24.18.0. The existing Round12/13 installer currently resolves node.exe from user PATH and accepts any Node >=22.5.0, while source-uat npm execution inherits ambient npm_config_* state. This work package authorizes a failure-first repair that makes the UAT candidate carry and verify the already-pinned Final Validation Node 22.23.1 runtime, uses that candidate-owned Node/npm for all source-UAT preparation and launch authority, and sanitizes ambient npm configuration so Microsoft node-pty's shipped win32-x64 prebuild seam remains authoritative instead of requiring end-user native compilation. The repair must reuse existing actions/setup-node, official Node runtime, upstream node-pty prebuild behavior, and tools/wp7/node-runtime-identity.js; it must not add a Yance downloader, require Visual Studio/Spectre components on the UAT machine, change Letta/node-pty/root dependency versions, or weaken npm/dependency integrity checks.

The generated UAT installer must verify and use the candidate-owned Node/npm runtime for dependency preparation, prelaunch gates, and source UAT launch; missing, modified, or wrong-version runtime bytes must fail closed before npm ci.

npm ci must not inherit ambient npm_config_* build/runtime/target/user configuration from the UAT machine; the install authority must provide an isolated controlled npm configuration while preserving the trusted dependency cache, frozen package-lock semantics, install scripts, and integrity verification.

Microsoft node-pty@1.1.0 win32-x64 packaged prebuilds must remain the mature OSS seam; the repair must not force native source compilation and must not require end-user Visual Studio, Windows SDK, or Spectre-mitigated libraries.
No Letta, node-pty, root package dependency, lockfile, Electron trust, Product source, or release-authority change is authorized.
